title: Braised Beef Short Ribs
summary: Beef short ribs slow-cooked in wine and stock until they melt in the mouth, with a rich, concentrated gravy. Serve with polenta or mashed potatoes.

steps.text: Preheat the oven to {temp:160/140}. Pat the short ribs dry and season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large, heavy-based pan over a high heat. Sear the short ribs on all sides until deeply browned, {timer:3-4} per side. Lift out the ribs and set aside.
Lower the heat to medium and add the onions, carrots, celery and garlic to the same pan. Sauté for {timer:8-10}, until the vegetables soften and start to colour.
Add the tomato paste and cook, stirring, for {timer:2-3}, until it darkens.
Pour in the red wine, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Let it reduce by half, {timer:5-7}.
Transfer the wine and vegetables to a large ovenproof dish or casserole. Nestle the short ribs into the vegetables.
Add beef stock until the ribs are completely submerged, then add the bay leaves and thyme.
Cover tightly with a lid or foil and braise in the oven for {timer:240} (4 hours), until the meat is falling off the bone.
Lift the ribs out carefully, as they will be very tender, and keep them warm.
Strain the braising liquid through a fine sieve, pressing the vegetables to extract all the flavour. Discard the solids.
Pour the liquid into a saucepan and bring to the boil. Reduce for {timer:15-20}, until thickened to a gravy. Season to taste.
Serve the short ribs with the reduced gravy, polenta or mashed potatoes, and grilled broccoli.

tips: The key to tender short ribs is low, slow cooking, so do not rush the braise. The meat should be tender enough to fall apart under a fork. Searing the ribs well adds a great deal of flavour to the sauce. The dish is even better made a day ahead: refrigerate it overnight, skim the fat from the surface, then reheat gently. The reduced gravy should be rich and glossy. For a traditional Italian finish, serve with soft polenta and a gremolata of lemon zest, parsley and garlic.
